newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end light pit trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end light pit trading mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended a session of light trading barely mixed, with most units showing little daily change.
Traders reported a few spurts of fairly active trade that enlivened a session of otherwise low-volume turnover.
In the Canadian dollar, traders said institutions bought a total of 674 nearby futures in two equal-sized batches through the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's "all-or-nothing" procedure.
The first purchase occurred at 0.7312 and the second was made at $0.7322, hitting buystops and threatening resistance near $0.7325, a floor broker said.
"It can move 30 ticks, and what have I got?" asked a floor broker at the CME. "It crawled up."
Daily volume on the price boards was estimated at roughly 5,500 for the Canadian dollar and 10,000 for the mark.
Currencies brushed off the 0.9-percent rise in retail sales during the first three weeks of August versus July, as reported by Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook.

Futures already had begun to weaken from morning firmness when the Conference Board reported that August U.S. consumer confidence rose to a six-year high of 109.4 from a revised 107.0 in July. It was expected to fall to 104.4.

Attention locked on Wednesday's Bank of Japan's quarterly Tankan business diffusion index that the broker said his firm expected to firm. "If it's much higher, we're in trouble," he added. "I think the dollar will lose a little bit."
The BoJ on Tuesday in its monthly report said Japan's economy is recovering moderately and the recovery is gradually gaining momentum, especially in business investment.

Sept yen rose $0.000002 to $0.009311, marks up $0.0003 at $0.6772, Swiss fr up $0.0003 at $0.8395, Sterling fell $0.0024 to $1.5544, Can dollar rose $0.0016 to $0.7316, Aussie dollar fell $0.0028 to $0.7872, Mexican peso rose $0.000350 to $0.131700. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
